articles.title: U2’s The Edge Wrote an ‘Elf’ Sequel, But It ‘Petered Out and Never Happened,’ Says Andy Richter
articles.summary: According to Andy Richter, U2’s the Edge penned a script for a sequel to “Elf” — but fans will likely never get to see (or read) it. On a recent episode of “Obsessed: The Podcast,” the actor explained that Shauna Robertson, who’d produced the original film, once received a message saying that the…
body: According to Andy Richter, U2 ’s the Edge penned a script for a sequel to “ Elf ” — but fans will likely never get to see (or read) it.

“Somebody reached out to her and said, ‘The Edge from U2 has written a sequel to ‘Elf,’ and he wants to talk to you about it,’” Richter said. “It’s the weirdest story, but apparently it was fully written. Somewhere in the world there is an Edge-penned ‘Elf 2’ out there… I would love for that to make the light of day. It never happened. It’s one of those things where she’s like, ‘All right, sure, I’ll meet him,’ and then it just petered out and never happened.”

And yet despite how beloved the holiday classic remains 23 years later, Richter is steadfast in the belief that a sequel isn’t necessary at this point. “I’m on the side of ‘Let it stand,’” he said. ”Just let ‘Elf’ be ‘Elf.’ You don’t have to use every part of the animal.”

He continued: “Now that time has passed, the movie has become so special that I think that people, rightfully so, are loath to mess with it because we all can think of movies that have been tarnished by their sequels. And this is so special and so perfect and so beloved… Why risk it?”
points: According to Andy Richter, U2’s the Edge penned a script for a sequel to “Elf” — but fans will likely never get to see (or read) it.

articles.title: ‘Club Kid’ Scene-Stealer Kirby Howell-Baptiste on Playing a Drugged-Up Party Girl Who Turns Jordan Firstman’s World Upside Down: She’s ‘A Complete Tornado’
articles.summary: “Should we do a bump?” It’s a line said, in various forms, numerous times across the first half of “Club Kid,” Jordan Firstman’s hedonistic and heartfelt coming-of-age comedy drama about a hard-partying New York club promoter suddenly forced to grapple with life and responsibilities.
body: “She’s a massive party girl — she never sleeps, she only parties,” says Brit actor Kirby Howell-Baptiste of how Edison was described to her. “She’s completely lost all social boundaries. The lifetime of drugs melted half of her brain away, and all her social cues and etiquette have gone.”
Howell-Baptiste’s etiquette-free Edison is only in “Club Kid” for a few minutes, but manages to steal the crucial scene in question from under the nose of writer, director and lead star Firstman.

Roughly quarter of the way into the film, she rocks up unannounced and chaotic, sporting green braids and oversized sunglasses, at the apartment lived in by Firstman’s nightclub promoter Peter (Firstman), with 10-year-old Arlo (Reggie Absolom) in tow. While wandering around the place like it’s her own, she reveals — in a hysterically matter-of-fact manner — that not only is Arlo his, but she’s brought the kid across from the U.K. to live with him permanently. Boom.

articles.title: French Cinema Is Thriving at Festivals but Facing an Uphill Battle in U.S. Theaters as Distributors Navigate a Shrinking Market
articles.summary: French cinema may be enjoying a golden run on the festival circuit and in the awards race, but getting those films into U.S. theaters, and persuading American audiences to buy tickets, has become an increasingly uphill battle.
body: The panel brought together Robert Aronson, executive VP of Cohen Media Group; John Gerrans, co-president of Strand Releasing; and Paul Hudson, CEO of Outsider Pictures, who have collectively brought hundreds of international films to American audiences.

The challenges extend well beyond French cinema. With fewer distributors acquiring independent films and arthouse theaters increasingly turning to mainstream Hollywood fare, even critically acclaimed movies are struggling to secure meaningful theatrical runs.

The definition of a French-language box office hit has also changed dramatically along with the health of the special market for most foreign-language films. Jean-Pierre Jeunet’s cult film “Amélie” grossed approximately $33 million domestically a quarter-century ago. By comparison, Justine Triet’s Palme d’Or winner “Anatomy of a Fall,” one of the most successful French films of the last five years which was handled by Neon and won an Oscar, earned around $5 million in the U.S..

articles.title: Bill Skarsgård Says He ‘Wasn’t Even Thrown Into the Mix’ to Be James Bond: ‘Maybe They Were Like, “We Can’t Do a Swede”’
articles.summary: Bill Skarsgård won’t be the next 007, but he would play a Bond villain. In a recent appearance on Josh Horowitz’s “Happy Sad Confused” podcast, Skarsgård revealed he wasn’t asked to test for Denis Villeneuve’s reboot. “They didn’t call me about James Bond.
body: Casting rumors for the new Bond have recently reached a fever pitch, with names like Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden swirling around. Most recently, Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult were revealed to have screen-tested for the role.
Skarsgård agreed with Horowitz that he wouldn’t want to sign on for a decade plus of playing 007. “That’s right,” he said. “Just want to go in and do one Mads Mikkelsen villain.”

“It’s not something that I’m actively looking for, but if I feel compelled to do something, yeah,” Skarsgård continued. “It’s the weird thing. A lot of people ask me, what goes into picking your roles or whatever and I don’t really know how to say it other than I feel drawn or compelled to. It’s something that you can’t really put your words on it and describe why it’s happening.”

He added: “But I’ve also noticed that I don’t want to become jaded. Which means that I think I could probably go long stretches without working and waiting for something to be compelling enough for me to work on.”

articles.title: Hollywood banks on Ebenezer to bring Johnny Depp in from the cold
articles.summary: Dickens character is actor’s first big studio role after years overshadowed by legal battles with ex-wife Amber Heard. “It’s good to be back,” Johnny Depp declares in the trailer for Ebenezer, in which he stars as Charles Dickens’s miserly Scrooge – his first big Hollywood studio production in…
body: The message is clear: this is Depp’s comeback, after years in which his career was overshadowed by legal battles with his former wife Amber Heard.

Paramount has made a point of invoking Depp’s most famous roles – the trailer opens with references to Captain Jack Sparrow, Edward Scissorhands and the Mad Hatter, before announcing: “The master of misfits returns.”
When the film opens on 13 November, it will be a test – not just of whether Depp can still sell cinema tickets, but whether Hollywood can restore him to the ranks of mainstream leading men.
“I think Ebenezer will serve as a bellwether for the industry as to Depp’s bankability,” said Robert Mitchell, the director of theatrical insights at Gower Street Analytics.

body: Yeoh is an actor who likes to figure things out for herself and, in the prep stages for Blade Runner 2099, the key question she thought about while building her character was, “What is it to be human? Are you born with humanity or does it come from the things you go through?”

As fans of Yeoh will know, however, the actor started out as a dancer, moved to martial arts movies in the 80s and is as robustly physical as any in Hollywood. An action star at heart, Yeoh is quick on her feet and unprecious in her outlook – so much so that, on occasion, she has found Hollywood a bit cautious compared with the wild west of the Hong Kong film industry she came up in as a young woman. “I’m tiny, I’m petite, five foot four,” she says, yet her ability to change her affect through movement is so intense, so persuasive, that, placed alongside Hunter Schafer, her much taller co-star in Blade Runner, “somehow you feel I loom over her”.

articles.title: Knicks defend Taylor Swift after players name her 'fakest celebrity fan'
articles.summary: The pop superstar's appearances at NBA games were deemed "a little performative" by New York Knicks point guards Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride.
body: The New York Knicks has defended superstar Taylor Swift, after players named her as the fakest celebrity fan.
"At the Knicks games, I would say it's very performative, cause like they just want to be seen at the game, they're not necessarily fans. Maybe Taylor Swift?" Kolek responded.
In May and June this year, Swift attended Game Three of the NBA Eastern Conference Finals in Cleveland and Game Four of the NBA Finals in New York City.
"I don't know if I've seen her at any other games," Kolak said.

articles.title: Walter Koenig Wanted A Star Trek: The Next Generation Role That Wasn't Pavel Chekov
articles.summary: Walter Koenig wanted to appear on Star Trek: The Next Generation without reprising his role as Pavel Chekov, and his idea was later used for a different show.
body: While "Star Trek: The Next Generation" is set 100 years after "Star Trek: The Original Series," some "TOS" cast members appeared on the show. In the pilot, "Encounter at Farpoint," a 137-year-old Dr. McCoy (DeForest Kelley) visits the Enterprise-D and gives Data (Brent Spiner) some sound advice: "You treat her like a lady, she'll always bring you home."

Later, in the Season 3 episode "Sarek," Mark Lenard guest-starred as the eponymous Vulcan ambassador, also known for being Spock's (Leonard Nimoy) father. Spock himself then appeared in the Season 5 two-parter "Reunification," where it's revealed he's moved to Romulus to try and bring the Vulcans and Romulans together again as one. After that, the former Enterprise Chief Engineer Scotty (James Doohan) appeared in the "Next Generation" Season 6 Episode "Relics," having spent several decades trapped in a Dyson sphere. Finally, Captain Kirk (William Shatner) teamed up with Captain Picard (Patrick Stewart) in the 1994 spin-off film "Star Trek Generations."

articles.title: Gilligan's Island Star Jim Backus Voiced One Of Animation's Most Famous Characters
articles.summary: Jim Backus is best known for playing 'The Millionaire' on Gilligan's Island, but he also voiced a famous animated character with deep pockets of his own.
body: Though he may not be a household name today, Jim Backus was a well known character actor in the mid-20th Century. Of course, his most recognizable role will forever remain Thurston Howell III from "Gilligan's Island," as Backus brought a suitably refined energy to the part of a New England patrician stranded alongside other societal archetypes in the South Pacific. But Backus' career stretched far beyond three seasons of a beloved CBS sitcom. Both prior to and after becoming trapped on the Isle, for instance, he voiced the animated character Quincy Magoo, better known as Mr. Magoo — a role he played from 1949 until 1977.

The actor's pre-Thurston Howell career was already impressive. Before "Gilligan's Island," Backus appeared opposite Clint Eastwood in the movie "Francis in the Navy," although he gained far more in the way of significant recognition for putting on an acting masterclass as the Stark family patriarch, Frank Stark, in the James Dean classic "Rebel Without a Cause." That likely would've gone down as his biggest non-"Gilligan's Island" role, too, if it weren't for the fact he voiced Mr. Magoo for some three decades.
points: Jim Backus is best known for playing 'The Millionaire' on Gilligan's Island, but he also voiced a famous animated character with deep pockets of his own.

articles.title: Connor Wood Reveals What Happened on 8th Avenue With Jennifer Lawrence in New Smoothie King Collab: “Missed My Moment” (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The 'Dancing With the Stars' contestant teamed up with Smoothie King to debut “Connor’s Paid Me No Mind Smoothie," a play on the trendy moment sparked by the Oscar winner.
body: Connor Wood is coming clean about what really led to Jennifer Lawrence ‘s viral comment about seeing him on 8th avenue and him paying her no mind.

“I think enough time has passed that I can break my silence about what happened on 8th avenue that day,” Wood said in a new video (watch below). “I was preoccupied that day. I was distracted. I missed my moment. I dropped the ball.”

“Not this time, OK, this time, I’m paying mind. I’m a changed man. I’ll never not pay attention again. My eyes are up. My mind is open. My body is nourished, right,” he said while holding his smoothie. Additional shots of Wood looking alert, walking around outside were shown, as a pedestrian even told him, “Oh hey, I saw you on 8th ave!”
“Connor’s Paid Me No Mind” smoothie features 26g of protein and 0g of added sugar per 20 oz. cup, made with whole strawberries and bananas plus electrolytes to support hydration.

articles.title: ‘Nobody Wants This’ Stars Hint at Season 4 and Declare Timothy Simons “the Lead of the Show Now”
articles.summary: Kristen Bell, Justine Lupe, Jackie Tohn and Simons united (minus Adam Brody) for a FYC conversation about the Netflix rom-com's latest batch of episodes.
body: On the same day that Nobody Wants This was renewed for a fourth season, the cast and crew came together to break down season three and tease what may be coming next.

The conversation began with a mention of the season four renewal, as Bell told the room, “I know a couple things which are really exciting, but I’m just excited to read the drafts.” Simons added that after Bell and Brody’s characters had a surprise wedding to end season three, “I personally am really excited to see the families’ reaction to that because it was very romantic, them getting married like on a lark at the ocean.”

“It was a lane that I don’t think either of us had ever really played in before,” the actor continued. “We got to be two sort of oddballs doing a romantic comedy; I didn’t have to be super smoky-eyed, I got to be a little bit of a funhouse-mirror version of a romantic lead.”

It seems to have worked out, with the episode being a breakout moment from season three. Bell gave her full endorsement, saying, “The whole New York episode I think is one of the best episodes of television that has ever been made. I was standing up watching the cut” and “my body was aching for them to be together.”
